name: public-browser

tools.name: virtual_desk
tools.description: List all open tabs with IDs, URLs and state. Call it first in every session, after a reconnect, or when unsure; reuse a listed tab ID instead of opening duplicates. Cheap, call liberally.

tools.name: view_page
tools.description: See what is on the page: text plus stable element refs for click/type/fill_form. Default filter 'interactive' lists actionable elements; for paragraphs or table cells call view_page(ref, filter: 'all'). Collapsed containers show as [eXX role, N items] — expand with view_page(ref: 'eXX', filter: 'all').

depth.description: Tree levels shown; indentation only, hidden sections need a click

filter.description: interactive | all | landmark | visual (bounds, click point, visibility)

max_tokens.description: Token budget; content downsampled. Omit for full output

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element by ref, CSS selector, visible text, or viewport x/y (canvas, pixel-precise targets). Dispatches real CDP mouse events. A click that opens a new tab is reported in the response. The DOM diff (NEW/REMOVED/CHANGED) arrives with the next page action, or here with wait_for_diff: true.

text.description: Visible text (a11y name); no view_page needed, prefers interactive

x.description: Viewport X in px; with y, not ref/selector

y.description: Viewport Y in px; use with x

wait_for_diff.description: Wait for the DOM diff before returning (default false, slower)

tools.name: type
tools.description: Type text into an input identified by ref or CSS selector. For 2+ fields use fill_form; for special keys (Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows) or shortcuts (Ctrl+K) use press_key.

tools.name: fill_form
tools.description: Fill a whole form in one call: text inputs, <select> (by value or visible label), checkboxes (boolean) and radio buttons. One round-trip; partial errors do not abort and each field reports its own status. On per-field errors call view_page and retry the failing fields.

value.description: string for text/select, boolean for checkbox/radio; number → string

fields.description: Each needs ref or selector plus value

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Press a key or shortcut (Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows, Ctrl+K). Optionally focus an element first via ref or selector.

key.description: Key to press, e.g. 'Enter'; printable chars as-is

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the press

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page, a container, or an element into view. Reports the position and content growth (scrollHeight delta — detects lazy-loaded content) and handles settle timing. Use container_ref/container_selector plus direction to scroll inside a container.

ref.description: Element ref to scroll into view

selector.description: CSS selector to scroll into view

container_ref.description: Scrollable container ref (scrolls it, not the page)

direction.description: up or down (default down); used when no ref/selector

amount.description: Pixels per scroll (default 500); only with direction

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag a source onto a target: HTML5 drag-and-drop (draggable lists, SortableJS, React DnD) and mouse drags (sliders, canvas, resize handles). Scrolls the source into view; says when no page reaction was detected. Source: from_ref/from_selector or from_x+from_y; target: to_ref/to_selector or to_x+to_y.

from_x.description: Source viewport X in px (with from_y)

to_x.description: Target viewport X in px (with to_y)

steps.description: Native mouseMoved events between press and release; minimum 5

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate the active tab to a URL, or action 'back' / 'reload' (all refs become stale after reload). Waits for settle. Overwrites the user's active tab — check virtual_desk first; the first call per session is redirected to virtual_desk.

settle_ms.description: Extra wait in ms after load (default 500)

tools.name: switch_tab
tools.description: Open a new tab, switch to a tab by ID (from virtual_desk), or close one. Prefer 'open' over navigate when the user's active tab must stay untouched. Refs from the previous tab are invalid afterwards — call view_page before acting.

url.description: URL for a new tab (open); default about:blank

tab.description: Tab ID or 1-based number (switch/close; close: active tab)

tools.name: tab_status
tools.description: Active tab's cached URL, title, ready state and errors — a cheap mid-workflow sanity check ('did my click navigate?'). Not for tab discovery or page content.

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Wait until a condition holds: element visible, page text present, URL match, network idle, or a JS expression true. Prefer condition 'text' over a JS expression for 'has the page said X yet'. assert: true checks once and fails instead of waiting.

selector.description: CSS selector or ref; required for condition 'element'

text.description: Substring of document.body.innerText, case-sensitive; required for condition 'text'

url.description: Substring of the page URL; required for condition 'url'

expression.description: Expression that should become true; required for condition 'js'

assert.description: Check once, fail if it does not hold; timeout 0, _meta.code 'assertion_failed'

timeout.description: Max wait in ms (default 10000; 0 when assert is true)

tools.name: observe
tools.description: Watch an element for changes instead of polling with MutationObserver/setInterval code in evaluate. collect: record text/attribute changes for 'duration' ms. until: wait for a condition, then optionally click at once (then_click). click_first fires the triggering action after the observer is armed, so nothing is missed.

selector.description: CSS selector or ref of the element to observe

duration.description: Collect window in ms (default 5000); exclusive with until

until.description: JS expression checked on each change, 'el' is the element, e.g. el.textContent === '8'

then_click.description: Selector or ref to click immediately when until holds

click_first.description: Selector or ref to click once the observer is armed

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Pixel-level screenshot (WebP, max 800px, <100KB). Only for canvas or chart content without DOM text, pixel-level rendering or animation checks, or when the user explicitly asks for a screenshot. Returns no refs and reads no text — that is view_page.

full_page.description: Capture the full scrollable page, not just the viewport

som.description: Overlay numbered labels matching view_page refs (Set-of-Mark)

tools.name: dom_snapshot
tools.description: Structured layout data: bounding boxes, computed styles, paint order, colors; refs match view_page. Only for spatial questions view_page cannot answer (is A above B? what color?).

ref.description: Element ref for a subtree snapshot

tools.name: handle_dialog
tools.description: Configure handling of alerts, confirms and prompts. Set it BEFORE triggering the action that opens the dialog. Uses CDP Page.javascriptDialogOpening, so it works even while the dialog blocks all JS.

action.description: accept or dismiss the next dialog; get_status: pending ones

text.description: Text entered into prompt dialogs (with action accept)

tools.name: file_upload
tools.description: Upload file(s) to an <input type='file'> identified by ref or CSS selector; file paths must be absolute.

ref.description: Element ref of the file input

selector.description: CSS selector of the file input; needed for hidden inputs (display:none, off-screen), which have no ref

path.description: Absolute path(s) of the file(s) to upload

tools.name: console_logs
tools.description: Read collected browser console logs; filter by level (info/warning/error/debug) and/or regex; optionally clear the buffer after reading.

tools.name: network_monitor
tools.description: Capture network requests via CDP, including those the page issues itself. Workflow: start → trigger the action → get(pattern: 'api').

action.description: start recording | get results | stop: return and clear

tools.name: download
tools.description: Wait for pending downloads or list this session's downloaded files. Downloads start by themselves when you click a download link or open a file URL (PDF, CSV, …); this tool never triggers them. download() waits for a pending download to finish; download({ action: 'list' }) returns at once.

action.description: status waits for pending downloads; list: history, never waits (use for polling)

timeout.description: Max wait in ms for pending downloads

settle.description: Ms to wait for a download to START before reporting none — Chrome fires downloadWillBegin a few ms after the click; 0 = instant

tools.name: configure_session
tools.description: View or set session defaults for recurring parameters (tab, timeout, …). Without params: show current defaults and auto-promote suggestions; autoPromote: true applies them. Set profile BEFORE any browser interaction to launch Chrome with a named profile.

defaults.description: Param name → default value; null removes a default

profile.description: Chrome profile name (list them with: public-browser profiles); restart: true switches mid-session

restart.description: Restart Chrome with the new profile even if running; closes all tabs

tools.name: run_plan
tools.description: Batch the next 2+ known actions (click, type, scroll, view_page chains) here instead of N separate calls: a sequence of tool steps, executed server-side in one call. Variables via vars and saveAs ($name), conditions (if), suspend/resume to ask the agent mid-plan, and errorStrategy abort | continue | capture_image.

saveAs.description: Save the result as $name for later steps

if.description: Run the step only if this expression is true, e.g. "$pageTitle === 'Login'"

condition.description: Suspend after the step if this $-expression is true

suspend.description: Pause here to ask the agent a question

steps.description: Tool steps to run in order

errorStrategy.description: abort stops at the first error; continue runs all steps; capture_image screenshots, then aborts

tools.name: batch_evaluate
tools.description: Visit several URLs in sequence and run the same JS expression on each. For controlled checks across known pages where view_page/run_plan would be too chatty; not for normal reading, clicking or form work.

evaluate_per_page.description: JS expression evaluated on each page

settle_ms.description: Wait in ms after each page load before evaluating

continue_on_error.description: Continue with the remaining URLs if one fails

tools.name: set_page_data
tools.description: Write a payload larger than 1 MB into window.__pb_data[key], chunked past the CDP 1 MB message limit. Source: inline (`data`) or file (absolute `path`, read as binary). The page reads window.__pb_data[key] (string or ArrayBuffer per encoding) and window.__pb_data[key + '__complete'] === true. Never write one key from parallel calls — they race. Under ~200 KB use evaluate; for a real <input type=file> use file_upload.

key.description: Property name under window.__pb_data (JS identifier, see pattern)

source.description: inline: pass data. file: pass an absolute path, read as binary

encoding.description: utf8 (inline default) keeps a string; binary (file default) gives an ArrayBuffer for FileReader/Blob/fetch; base64 keeps the base64 string

chunkSize.description: Raw bytes per chunk before base64 (default 500000; max 700000)

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Run JavaScript in the page. Good uses: computation, style mutations (.style.X = ..., classList), shadow-root traversal, in-page fetch(), app-specific side effects no dedicated tool covers. Scope is shared between calls; top-level const/let/class are wrapped in an IIFE. If/else blocks may return undefined — use a ternary or an explicit return.

expression.description: JavaScript code to execute in the page context

instructions:
Public Browser controls a real Chrome browser via CDP.

Workflow: virtual_desk → navigate (to open a page) → view_page (read) → click/type/fill_form (act) → view_page (verify the result).

CRITICAL — view_page vs capture_image:
- To see what is on the page: ALWAYS call view_page. It returns text + element refs for click/type.
- capture_image is ONLY for CSS layout checks, canvas content, or when the user explicitly asks for a screenshot.
- Do NOT call capture_image to read text, find buttons, check errors, or see page state — that is view_page.
- capture_image cannot return element refs, so you cannot click anything you see in it.

Other rules:
- After every interaction, use view_page again to verify the result before proceeding.
- Element targets: prefer the ref from the last view_page (e.g. 'e5'); a CSS selector is the fallback. Refs go stale after navigate, reload or switch_tab — call view_page again before acting on the new page.
- fill_form beats multiple type calls for any form with 2+ fields.
- For multi-step workflows, use run_plan to execute N steps in one call. Whenever the next 2+ actions are known (click → click, click → type → view_page), send them as ONE run_plan, not separate calls.
- evaluate is for JS computation and style mutations (.style.X = ...) — not for CSS reading, element discovery, scrolling, dialogs or network capture: dom_snapshot, view_page, scroll, handle_dialog and network_monitor cover those.
- Avoid evaluate as default recovery after click/type errors — call view_page for fresh refs and retry with the dedicated tool. Patching via evaluate (querySelector().click(), element.value = ...) bypasses the CDP pointer chain and framework listeners (React, Vue) and hides real bugs; the only exception is a test that deliberately targets synthetic JS events.
- Responses of type and fill_form carry a DOM diff (NEW/REMOVED/CHANGED lines); click's diff arrives with the next page action unless wait_for_diff: true. Read it as the success signal instead of re-checking state with evaluate.

Script API: `pip install publicbrowser` gives you a Python library for deterministic browser automation without an LLM. Scripts route through the same tool handlers as MCP (Shared Core). Usage: `from publicbrowser import Chrome; chrome = Chrome.connect(); page = chrome.new_page()` — then `page.navigate()`, `page.click()`, `page.fill()`, `page.evaluate()` etc. Auto-starts the server. Add `--script` to the MCP args for parallel MCP + Script access.
